_comment: Target `main` branch-protection policy for this repository. Apply with:
gh api -X PUT repos/cinatra-ai/cinatra/branches/main/protection \
--input .github/branch-protections.json
Requires Code Owner review + the listed status checks, and forbids
force-pushes and branch deletion. Root CODEOWNERS maps
`* @groganz @megajustice`, so the Code Owner requirement binds (there is no
`@cinatra-ai/maintainers` team yet; if one is created, repoint CODEOWNERS and
this note together). Review and adjust the required-check contexts if those
workflows are renamed.
required_approving_review_count is 0 (NOT 1): the merge model is owner
--admin self-merge + the machine verification-record arm + a bot PR for any
high-risk change the owner approves (the owner cannot self-approve their own
PR, so a count of 1 would block routine owner merges). The org
`baseline-protection` ruleset also sets count 0; require_code_owner_reviews
stays true so the CODEOWNERS gate still binds. The `proof` context is the
works-after-proof.yml upgrade gate (job `proof`).
NOTE: a `v*` tag triggers a production deploy (build-image.yml -> ops), so
tag/release creation must be restricted to maintainers SEPARATELY (Settings ->
Tags, or a `v*` tag protection rule) — branch protection does not cover tags.
required_status_checks.strict is false (NOT true): requiring branches to be
up to date before merging was deliberately dropped (owner decision,
2026-07-06, merge-train livelock fix, Path B kept over a merge queue). Review
provenance now binds to the change CONTENT (the content/diff-binding
attribution gate), so a mechanical update-branch no longer invalidates an
approval, and the mandatory post-merge verification on the real merged SHA
catches semantic conflicts that an up-to-date requirement would have. If a
GitHub merge queue is ever enabled, revisit this note and the setting
together.
The `gates` and `gates-pnpm` contexts are gates.yml, the consolidated
micro-gate runner: one job per dependency class, one STEP per source gate.
They are required as a WHOLE because there is no finer handle. The
product-tree hygiene guard, the docs-tree guard, the route bans and the
policy gates all live as steps inside those two jobs, so a red step is only
reachable as a red `gates` / `gates-pnpm` check. gates.yml runs on every
pull_request, merge_group and push to main, with no `paths:` filter and no
job-level `if:`, so both contexts always report and neither can hang a PR by
never running. Adding a context here does NOT change the live protection:
re-apply this file with the `gh api -X PUT` command at the top once this
merges, or the new requirement exists only on paper.
The `design-pin-drift` context is the design-pin-drift job in gates.yml
(cinatra#3057 rollout step b): its own job, not a step in `gates`, so it can
be listed as a separate required context. Its workflow triggers on every
pull_request, merge_group, push to main and workflow_dispatch with no paths
filter, so the context always reports and cannot hang a PR by never running.
Once required, a pull request touching none of the mapped paths in
scripts/ci/design-pin-drift.paths.json stays green (warning annotation, exit
0); a pull request touching a drifted pin's mapped paths goes red until that
pin is adopted. See docs/internals/contracts/design-conformance-pin-drift.md.
Adding a context here does NOT change the live protection: re-apply this file
with the `gh api -X PUT` command at the top once this merges, or the new
requirement exists only on paper.
